newsitem.title: UK: North Sea Brent trades weaker, other grades firm.
newsitem.headline: North Sea Brent trades weaker, other grades firm.

text.p: A wet Brent cargo was traded weaker than last week's levels late on Monday, but differentials for other North Sea grades were still talked firm, traders said.
A Brent cargo loading Dec 20-22 was bought by a European major at Jan Brent +22.5 cents, after last trading on Thursday at a Dated related price equivalent to around Jan Brent +35/+40.
"As we move towards January, logically it has to start coming off," said one trader.
But traders said that transatlantic arbitrage opportunities were likely to keep a floor under prices.
Dealers said that a Wall Street trader, the keeper of one of two Brent dates today, was still thought likely to be working a VLCC to the U.S.
NYMEX Jan crude extended its premium over Jan Brent futures on Monday to $1.21 a barrel by 1830 GMT.
The other Brent cargo nominated from the paper chains on Monday, was kept by equity holder Murphy.
A 600,000 barrel Oseberg cargo, loading Dec 28-30, was traded at a firm Dated Brent +50 cents after a Jan 1-5 cargo changed hands on Friday at Dated Brent +48 cents.
The sale left only a handful of December-loading cargoes still unsold, although traders said that attention had now turned to January barrels.
"Most people have done their Christmas buying," said one trader. "(For December barrels) we'll probably won't be seeing much more buying except for optimising purposes now."
The Brent paper market was softer, with the Jan/Feb intermonth spread traded lower at +61 and +60 cents late in the day.
Jan Brent paper was talked lower in line with IPE futures which were trading 65 cents down at $23.89 a barrel at 1843 GMT.
